import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a figure with subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis: Key Specifications and Trends', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

# 1. Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type (Top Left)
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sensor_types = df['sensor_type'].unique()
colors = sns.color_palette('husl', len(sensor_types))
for i, sensor in enumerate(sensor_types):
    data = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(data['megapixels'], data['price_usd'], alpha=0.6, s=50, 
                label=sensor, color=colors[i])
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', fontsize=9)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 2. Average Price by Brand (Top Right)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
brand_price = df.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
bars = ax2.barh(brand_price.index, brand_price.values, color=sns.color_palette('viridis', len(brand_price)))
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Average Camera Price by Brand', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')
for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
    width = bar.get_width()
    ax2.text(width, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'${width:.0f}', 
             ha='left', va='center', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')

# 3. Camera Evolution: Year vs Megapixels with 4K capability (Bottom Left)
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
video_4k = df[df['has_video_4k'] == 1]
no_video_4k = df[df['has_video_4k'] == 0]
ax3.scatter(no_video_4k['model_year'], no_video_4k['megapixels'], alpha=0.5, s=40, 
           label='No 4K Video', color='lightcoral')
ax3.scatter(video_4k['model_year'], video_4k['megapixels'], alpha=0.5, s=40, 
           label='4K Video', color='steelblue')
ax3.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_title('Camera Technology Evolution: Megapixels & 4K Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(fontsize=10)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 4. Body Type Distribution with 4K capability (Bottom Right)
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=ax4, color=['lightcoral', 'steelblue'], width=0.7)
ax4.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_title('Camera Body Type Distribution by 4K Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(['No 4K Video', '4K Video'], fontsize=10)
ax4.set_xticklabels(ax4.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha='right')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
